article.title: Connect your own provider account
article.excerpt: Bring-your-own-account keeps the agreement, the sender reputation and the invoice with your CPaaS provider. Here is how to connect one, and what changes once you do.

p: You connect an account you already hold. The platform stores the credentials you paste, routes through your account, and never becomes the party your provider invoices.
This is the difference that matters commercially: the pricing you negotiated, the sender numbers you already registered, and the delivery reputation you have built all stay where they are.
sections.scope: The connectable set is whatever the console lists when you add a connection — on SMS, email and WhatsApp alike. A provider outside that list cannot be connected yet: register it as a request from the console so it is counted rather than lost.

sections.h: Which credentials the SMS providers expect
p: Every provider asks for a different pair. The console labels every field and refuses to save until all required fields are present. The email and WhatsApp providers each have their own field list on their page under Integrations.

head: Provider
Credentials
rows: Account SID + Auth Token (account-level, not an API key pair)

steps.p: Channels → Add connection, then choose the provider type.
Use the field labels above as a checklist. Nothing is sent anywhere until you save.
The connection appears in the list. Its status becomes ACTIVE once the platform has accepted the credentials.

sections.note: Credentials are encrypted before they are stored and are never shown in full again. Copy them from your provider dashboard if you need to check them later.

sections.h: What ACTIVE does and does not mean
p: ACTIVE means the credentials validated. It does not promise that a given sender number is accepted by the provider, or that a destination country is reachable on that route.
Those refusals surface per message, as a failed status with an error code — see "Messages that fail with an error code".
A masked credential field is not a value you have to retype. Editing any field on the form re-encrypts only what you actually changed, so the stored secret survives an unrelated edit.
Removing a connection takes its sender numbers out of the rotation. An API key bound to it will have one fewer channel to send over — and a key left with no bound channel is rejected at send time.
